web.title: Support Tool Security Checklist (SOC2, SSO)
web.description: Checklist for SOC 2 Type II, enterprise SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, immutable audit logs, and RBAC controls buyers require.
snippets: This layer of security is a critical focus for SOC 2 audits, as access control issues are among the most common findings [10]. Poorly designed RBAC doesn’t just lead to compliance headaches – it opens the door to data breaches, which cost businesses an average of $4.4 million [12].

Features like Enterprise SSO (SAML 2.0/OIDC) offer centralized access control, while SCIM helps automate user deprovisioning, reducing the risk of orphaned accounts. Additionally, detailed audit logs support swift incident response, and properly implemented RBAC ensures permissions are enforced directly at the API layer [1].

To confirm that RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) is enforced on the server side, you need to ensure that permissions are checked in the backend, not just within the user interface. One way to test this is by attempting restricted actions through API calls or direct server requests using a role that doesn’t have the necessary permissions.
Security is now a dealbreaker for support tools. Enterprise buyers demand SOC 2 Type II certification, SSO, detailed activity logs, and RBAC.
